record.title: Lower-bound conjecture for diamond-saturated families avoiding the extremes
record.statement:
Let $n$ be a positive integer, let $\mathcal{B}_n$ be the Boolean lattice, and let $\mathcal{F}\subseteq\mathcal{B}_n$ be an induced-$\mathcal{D}_2$-saturated family that avoids both $\emptyset$ and $[n]$. **Lower-bound conjecture for diamond-saturated families avoiding the extremes.** There exists a universal constant $c>0$ such that

$$
2n-c\leq |\mathcal{F}|.
$$

The conjecture seeks a stronger lower bound for induced-$\mathcal{D}_2$-saturated families avoiding the two extreme sets; the source gives a construction of size $2n$ and presents this lower bound as an open question.
record.source_name: Michael Ferrara, Bill Kay, Lucas Kramer, Ryan R. Martin, Benjamin Reiniger, Heather C. Smith and Eric Sullivan, “The Saturation Number of Induced Subposets of the Boolean Lattice”, arXiv:1701.03010 (2017).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1701.03010

Status: **open** according to the source (as of January 2017). “More generally, there are many open questions in this subject.”

record.title: Distinct leverage centralities in Cartesian powers of path powers
record.statement:
Let $P_n^k$ denote the $k$th power of the path graph on $n$ vertices, and let

$$
G=P_n^k\mathbin{\square}\cdots\mathbin{\square}P_n^k
$$

be the Cartesian product of $m$ copies of $P_n^k$, with $n\geq 4k+1$. The **leverage-centrality count conjecture.** The number of distinct leverage centralities in $G$ is

$$
\binom{m+k+1}{k+1}.
$$

The authors verified the analogous count computationally for small values of $m$ and $k$, and the claim seeks the general formula for these Cartesian products.
record.source_name: Roger Vargas,, Abigail Waldron, Anika Sharma, Rigoberto Flórez and Darren A. Narayan, “A Graph Theoretic Analysis of Leverage Centrality”, arXiv:1701.04790 (2017).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1701.04790

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of January 2017).

record.title: Existence of nice nef partitions and toric Landau–Ginzburg models for weighted Fano complete intersections
record.statement:
Let $X$ be a smooth well formed Fano weighted complete intersection. A **nice nef partition conjecture** asserts that there exists a nice nef partition for $X$, and that $X$ has a toric Landau--Ginzburg model.

The preceding results establish this assertion for smooth well formed Fano weighted hypersurfaces and for smooth well formed Fano weighted complete intersections of codimension $2$. The conjecture would extend the existence of toric Landau--Ginzburg models to all smooth well formed Fano weighted complete intersections.
record.source_name: Victor Przyjalkowski and Constantin Shramov, “Nef partitions for codimension 2 weighted complete intersections”, arXiv:1702.00431 (2018).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1702.00431

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of February 2017).

record.title: Aleksandrov–Buryak–Tessler conjecture for the extended refined partition function
record.statement:
Let $N$ be any value for which the formal series are defined, let $\tau^{o,\mathrm{ext}}_N$ be the extended refined open partition function, and let $\tau_N$ be the Kontsevich–Penner tau-function. Use the formal variables $t_i$ and $s_i$ and make the substitutions

$$
T_{2i+1}=\frac{t_i}{(2i+1)!!},\qquad T_{2i+2}=\frac{s_i}{2^{i+1}(i+1)!}.
$$

**Extended refined Kontsevich–Penner conjecture.** For any $N$ we have

$$
\tau^{o,\mathrm{ext}}_N=\left.\tau_N\right|_{\substack{T_{2i+1}=\frac{t_i}{(2i+1)!!},\\T_{2i+2}=\frac{s_i}{2^{i+1}(i+1)!}.}}
$$

The equality is known for $N=1$ and the source states that the conjecture is proved in genus $0$ and $1$; it remains open in general.
record.source_name: Alexander Alexandrov, Alexandr Buryak and Ran J. Tessler, “Refined open intersection numbers and the Kontsevich-Penner matrix model”, arXiv:1702.02319 (2017).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1702.02319

Status: **solved** according to the source (as of February 2017).

record.title: Eulerian edge-refinement conjecture for sphere embeddings
record.statement:
Let $G$ be a $d$-sphere with $d\geq 2$ and let $H$ be a $(d+1)$-sphere containing $G$ as a subgraph. An **edge refinement** inserts a vertex into an edge and joins it to the common neighbors of the edge's endpoints. A graph is **Eulerian** when the relevant simplex degrees are even.

**Eulerian edge-refinement conjecture.** It is possible to edge refine $H$, using only edges different from those of $G$, so that the modified $H$ becomes Eulerian.

The conjecture is proposed as a sufficient condition for the sphere coloring conjecture: an Eulerian host would provide a coloring of the embedded sphere with $d+1$ or $d+2$ colors. The source gives no resolution and notes that the higher-dimensional cases remain to be investigated.
record.source_name: Oliver Knill, “Eulerian edge refinements, geodesics, billiards and sphere coloring”, arXiv:1808.07207 (2018).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1808.07207

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of August 2018).

record.title: Banica's universal flat matrix model conjecture for quantum permutation groups
record.statement:
Let $S_N^+$ be the quantum permutation group, and let $X_N$ be the compact space of $N\times N$ matrices $P=(P_{ij})$ whose entries are rank-one projections in $M_N(\mathbb C)$ satisfying

$$
\sum_jP_{ij}=1=\sum_iP_{ij}.
$$

The universal flat matrix model is the representation

$$
\pi:\mathcal A(S_N^+)\to M_N(C(X_N)),\qquad \pi(u_{ij})=\{P\mapsto P_{ij}\}.
$$

A representation is **faithful** when it is injective, and **inner faithful** when its kernel contains no non-trivial Hopf $\ast$-ideals. **Universal flat matrix model conjecture.** The universal flat matrix model is faithful for $N=4$ and inner faithful for $N\geq5$. The conjecture is attributed to Banica; the source does not provide evidence of resolution.
record.source_name: Michael Brannan, Alexandru Chirvasitu and Amaury Freslon, “Topological generation and matrix models for quantum reflection groups”, arXiv:1808.08611 (2018).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1808.08611

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of August 2018).

record.title: Mountain-end anchored packing conjecture
record.statement:
Consider a mountain permutation on the points, and suppose it starts with $m$ and ends with $(m-1,m-2,\ldots,1)$ for some $m\leq n$. Let $k$ be the proportion of the rectangular region with opposite vertices $P_1$ and $(x_{n-m+1},1)$ that can be filled, where $k>\frac12$. **Mountain-end conjecture.** Under these assumptions, one can fill at least

$$
\frac{1}{2}+\frac{1}{2\left(m+\frac{1}{2k-1}\right)}
$$

of the entire square. This claim is proposed as a strengthening for mountain permutations and would imply the lower bound $\frac12+\frac{1}{2n}$ for their optimal area; the source proves only the weaker half-area bound for mountain permutations.
record.source_name: Vincent Bian, “Special Configurations in Anchored Rectangle Packings”, arXiv:1809.01769 (2018).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1809.01769

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of September 2018).

record.title: The monotonicity conjecture for exceptional-word ratios
record.statement:
For each positive integer $m$, let $\mathcal E_m$ be the set of exceptional normalized words of length $m$, and let $\mathcal{NW}_m$ be the set of normalized words of length $m$. Here, a word is **exceptional** when its hare-fertility exceeds its tortoise-fertility. **The monotonicity conjecture for exceptional-word ratios.** The numbers

$$
\frac{|\mathcal E_m|}{|\mathcal{NW}_m|}
$$

are increasing in $m$. The paper reports computed values for $m=7,8,9$ and observes that, if the conjecture holds, the limiting ratio exists; its value remains to be determined.
record.source_name: Colin Defant and Noah Kravitz, “Stack-sorting for Words”, arXiv:1809.09158 (2018).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1809.09158

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of September 2018).

record.title: Samotij's theorem analog for projective cubes in $\mathbb{Z}_{2^n}$
record.statement: Let $n\geq k\geq 2$ and let $M$ be an integer. A family $\mathcal{F}\subseteq\mathbb{Z}_{2^n}$ has size $|\mathcal{F}|=M$, and centred families are defined by taking initial layers completely and later layers empty, with at most one layer partially filled. **Analog of Samotij's theorem.** Among all families of size $M$, centred families minimise the number of $2^k$-cubes. The paper identifies this as a main conjecture; no resolution is supplied.
record.source_name: Jason Long and Adam Zsolt Wagner, “The largest projective cube-free subsets of Z_2^n”, arXiv:1810.01225 (2018).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1810.01225

Status: **open** according to the source (as of October 2018). “Some further open questions and conjectures are given in Section .”

record.title: The Alishahi–Dowlin spectral sequence conjecture from Khovanov homology to knot Floer homology
record.statement:
Let $K$ be a knot in $S^{3}$. The Khovanov homology of $K$ and the knot Floer homology of $K$ are the endpoints of a conjectural spectral sequence.

**Alishahi–Dowlin spectral sequence conjecture.** There is a spectral sequence from the Khovanov homology of $K$ to the knot Floer homology of $K$.

This conjecture would relate two link homology theories that are defined by substantially different methods and appear to contain overlapping information. The paper constructs a filtered complex whose $E_{2}$ page is Khovanov homology and whose total homology is a link invariant, but the identification of its total homology with $mathit{\delta}$-graded knot Floer homology is conjectural.
record.source_name: Akram Alishahi and Nathan Dowlin, “A link invariant related to Khovanov homology and knot Floer homology”, arXiv:1810.13406 (2018).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1810.13406

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of October 2018).

record.title: Closed-form maximal Randić energy conjecture for selected orders
record.statement:
Let $G$ be a connected graph on $n$ vertices, and let $S^p$ and $DS^{p,q}$ denote the sun and double-sun graphs used in the source. Let $E_{\mathcal{L}}$ denote the normalized Laplacian energy. **Closed-form maximal Randić energy conjecture.** For odd $k\geq 3$,

$$
RE(G) \leq \begin{cases} RE(S^p)=E_{\mathcal{L}}(S^p)&\text{if $n=k$}\\ RE(DS^{p,p})=E_{\mathcal{L}}(D^{p,p-1})&\text{if $n=2k$}\\ RE(DS^{p,p-1})=E_{\mathcal{L}}(D^{p,p-1})&\text{if $n=2k+2$} \end{cases}
$$

The source presents this as a closed-form rewriting of the maximal Randić-energy conjecture after computing characteristic polynomials and energies for the relevant sun and balanced double-sun graphs. The general assertion remains unresolved in the supplied text.
record.source_name: Luiz Emilio Allem, Gonzalo Molina and Adrián Pastine, “Short note on Randić energy”, arXiv:1811.08776 (2018).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1811.08776

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of November 2018).

record.title: Uniqueness of local moves preserving electrical equivalence in punctured-disk networks
record.statement:
Let an rnpd be a resistor network embedded in a disk with exactly one boundary vertex placed inside the disk, and let two such graphs be electrically equivalent when they have the same response matrix. The paper lists local moves on these networks, including the moves introduced in this work.

**Local-move completeness conjecture.** Any two electrically equivalent graphs associated to rnpds are connected by the local moves stated in this section.

This would give a complete classification of the local transformations preserving electrical equivalence for resistor networks in a punctured disk. The source presents the assertion as a conjecture and provides no resolution.
record.source_name: Yulia Alexandr, Brian Burks, Sunita Chepuri and Patricia Commins, “Recovering Conductances of Resistor Networks in a Punctured Disk”, arXiv:1812.01517 (2018).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1812.01517

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of December 2018).

record.title: Sullivan's compromise conjectures for the second neighbourhood
record.statement:
Let $D$ be an oriented graph. For a vertex $x$ of $D$, write $d^{+}(x)$ and $d^{-}(x)$ for its out-degree and in-degree, respectively, and let $d^{++}(x)$ denote the number of vertices at directed distance exactly 2 from $x$.

**Sullivan's compromise conjectures.** Every oriented graph $D$ has a vertex $x$ satisfying at least one of the following two assertions:

$$
d^{++}(x)\geq d^{-}(x),
$$

or

$$
d^{++}(x)+d^{+}(x)\geq 2d^{-}(x).
$$

These are weaker alternatives to Seymour's Second Neighbourhood Conjecture. The source attributes them to Sullivan, but the supplied material does not establish whether either conjecture has been resolved.
record.source_name: Ruijuan Li and Juanjuan Liang, “The second out-neighbourhood for local tournaments”, arXiv:1812.01800 (2018).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1812.01800

Status: **open** according to the source (as of December 2018). “In 1990, Seymour proposed the following conjecture which is one of the most interesting and challenging open questions concerning oriented graphs.”

record.title: The final-matrix Sierpinski-triangle conjecture
record.statement:
Let $FM_n^{-}(x,y)$ be the negative final-matrix value and let $\mathrm{ST}_n$ be defined recursively by $\mathrm{ST}_0=(1,1)$ and

$$
(x,y)\in\mathrm{ST}_{n+1}\iff ((x)_{2^n},(y)_{2^n})\in\mathrm{ST}_n\text{ and }(x\leq2^n\text{ or }y>2^n).
$$

**Final-matrix Sierpinski-triangle conjecture.** Suppose $n\geq0$ and $\ell\leq x*y$ in $A_n$. Then:

1. If $M_n(x,y,\ell)>0$, then $(x*M_n(x,y,\ell),\ell)\in\mathrm{ST}_n$.
2. If $M_n(x,y,\ell)<0$, then $(-M_n(x,y,\ell),\ell)\in\mathrm{ST}_n$.

The claim formalizes the observed Sierpinski-triangle pattern in the final matrices, which the excerpt describes as unproved and important for understanding the combinatorial complexity of multigenic Laver tables.
record.source_name: Joseph Van Name, “Generalizations of Laver tables”, arXiv:1812.02761 (2018).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1812.02761

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of December 2018).

record.title: Leaf-sensitive oriented-tree universality conjecture
record.statement: A digraph is **$k$-universal** if it is contained in every digraph with chromatic number $k$. An **oriented tree** is an orientation of an undirected tree, and a leaf is a vertex of degree one in its underlying tree. **Leaf-sensitive universality conjecture.** Every oriented tree of order $n$ with $k$ leaves is $(n+k-1)$-universal. This is proposed as the universality analogue of the leaf-sensitive unavoidability conjecture, and no resolution is given in the source.
record.source_name: François Dross and Frédéric Havet, “On the unavoidability of oriented trees”, arXiv:1812.05167 (2018).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1812.05167

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of December 2018).

record.title: Nonexistence conjecture for superlinear elliptic inequalities on weighted graphs
record.statement:
Let $(V,\b5)$ be a weighted graph, let $o\in V$, and let $\sigma>1$. A nonnegative solution $u$ of the elliptic inequality

$$
\Delta u+u^{\sigma}\leq 0
$$

is a function on $V$ satisfying this inequality, where $B(o,n)$ denotes the ball of radius $n$ centered at $o$ and $\mu(B(o,n))$ its weighted volume. **Nonexistence conjecture.** If

$$
\sum_{n=1}^{\infty}\frac{n^{2\sigma-1}}{\mu(B(o,n))^{\sigma-1}}=\infty,
$$

then the only nonnegative solution to the elliptic inequality is identically zero. This would sharpen the stated nonexistence theorem by removing condition $(p_0)$, whose necessity is not known.
record.source_name: Qingsong Gu, Xueping Huang and Yuhua Sun, “Superlinear elliptic inequalities on weighted graphs”, arXiv:2201.06397 (2022).
record.references:
**2 papers in this index state this conjecture** (2018–2022). The statement above is taken from the most recent of them; the others are [arXiv:1810.03055](https://arxiv.org/abs/1810.03055).

Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2201.06397

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of January 2022).

record.title: The local antimagic chromatic number of joins of disjoint paths with a universal vertex
record.statement:
Let $P_n$ be the path on $n$ vertices, let $mP_n$ denote the disjoint union of $m$ copies of $P_n$, let $K_1$ be a single vertex, and let $\chi_{la}(G)$ denote the local antimagic chromatic number of a graph $G$. **The conjecture.** For $m\ge 2$ and $n\ge 2$, 

$$
\chi_{la}(mP_n \vee K_1)=3.
$$

This claim concerns a broad family of joins of disjoint paths with a universal vertex. The supplied text presents it as a statement in the conclusion and open-problems discussion, without indicating whether it has been proved or disproved.
record.source_name: Gee-Choon Lau, Wai Chee Shiu, K. Premalatha and M. Nalliah, “Constructions of local antimagic 3-colorable graphs of fixed odd size | matrix approach”, arXiv:2403.16484 (2024).
record.references:
**2 papers in this index state this conjecture** (2018–2024). The statement above is taken from the most recent of them; the others are [arXiv:1805.04801](https://arxiv.org/abs/1805.04801).

Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2403.16484

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of March 2024).

record.title: Máčajová–Škoviera odd-cut conjecture for bridgeless cubic graphs
record.statement: Let $G$ be a bridgeless cubic graph. A **perfect matching** is a set of edges meeting every vertex exactly once, and an **edge-cut** is the set of edges joining a vertex subset to its complement. **Máčajová–Škoviera conjecture.** Every bridgeless cubic graph has two perfect matchings such that their intersection does not contain an edge-cut of odd cardinality. This is one of the weaker statements implied by the Berge–Fulkerson conjecture and is stated in the source as having been proved by Kardoš, Máčajová and Zerafa.
record.source_name: Jan Goedgebeur, Davide Mattiolo, Giuseppe Mazzuoccolo, Jarne Renders, Luca Toffanetti and Isaak H. Wolf, “On the existence of factors intersecting sets of cycles in regular graphs”, arXiv:2411.09806 (2026).
record.references:
**2 papers in this index state this conjecture** (2018–2024). The statement above is taken from the most recent of them; the others are [arXiv:1811.08363](https://arxiv.org/abs/1811.08363).

Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2411.09806

Status: **solved** according to the source (as of November 2024). “It is proved in that Conjecture reduces to non-$3$-edge-colorable cubic graphs which are cyclically $5$-edge-connected.”

record.title: Merzon–Smirnov's layered-permutation conjecture for maximal Schubert specialization
record.statement:
For $n\geq 1$, define

$$
\alpha_n=\max\{\nu_w\colon w\in S_n\},
$$

where $\nu_w=\mathfrak{S}_w(x)|_{x_i=1}$. A **layered permutation** $w(b_1,\ldots,b_k)$ is the concatenation of decreasing blocks on consecutive intervals, where $b_1+\cdots+b_k=n$. **Merzon–Smirnov's conjecture.** For $n\geq 1$, the permutations in $S_n$ attaining $\alpha_n$ are layered permutations. The conjecture identifies the maximizers of the principal specialization; the source presents it as a prediction of Merzon and Smirnov.
record.source_name: Peter L. Guo and Zhuowei Lin, “Schubert polynomials and patterns in permutations”, arXiv:2412.02932 (2024).
record.references:
**3 papers in this index state this conjecture** (2018–2024). The statement above is taken from the most recent of them; the others are [arXiv:2311.04487](https://arxiv.org/abs/2311.04487), [arXiv:1805.04341](https://arxiv.org/abs/1805.04341).

Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2412.02932

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of December 2024).

record.title: Nonnegativity conjecture for the summed edge-deletion gamma-polynomial
record.statement:
Let $G=(V,E)$ be a 2-connected graph. For each edge $ij\in E$, set $c^{ij}(t):=h^*_{P_G}(t)-h^*_{P_{G\setminus ij}}(t)$, and let $\gamma(c^{ij}(t))$ denote the $\gamma$-polynomial associated with this palindromic difference. Define

$$
Z_G(t):=\sum_{ij\in E}\gamma(c^{ij}(t))=\sum_{ij\in E}\gamma\bigl(h^*_{P_G}(t)-h^*_{P_{G\setminus ij}}(t)\bigr)=\sum_{ij\in E}\bigl(\gamma_{P_G}(t)-\gamma_{P_{G\setminus ij}}(t)\bigr).
$$

**Summed edge-deletion nonnegativity conjecture.** The polynomial $Z_G(t)$ has nonnegative coefficients. This is proposed as a stronger statement whose gamma-nonnegativity would imply the existence of an edge with gamma-nonnegative deletion difference; the supplied text gives no resolution status.
record.source_name: Giulia Codenotti, Roberto Riccardi and Lorenzo Venturello, “The number of edges of a symmetric edge polytope”, arXiv:2512.16572 (2026).
record.references:
**2 papers in this index state this conjecture** (2018–2025). The statement above is taken from the most recent of them; the others are [arXiv:1809.00575](https://arxiv.org/abs/1809.00575).

Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2512.16572

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of December 2025).
